business_problem: Repsol wanted to measure whether generative AI could reduce time spent on routine knowledge work such as finding information, summarizing documents, drawing conclusions, comparing supplier proposals, and preparing presentations, while improving document quality and employee experience.
solution_summary: Repsol ran a 600-person, four-month pilot of Microsoft 365 Copilot after training participants to use the assistant in daily work. The implementation placed Microsoft 365 Copilot inside Word, Excel, and Teams, where employees could issue natural-language prompts for tasks such as drafting supplier emails, summarizing recorded meetings, comparing supplier proposals, analyzing information, and preparing presentations. According to the source, Copilot combines large language model capabilities with company data held in the cloud and information available on the Internet, while honoring each user's existing access permissions so responses are limited to content the employee is authorized to see. Repsol also describes a broader rollout of Microsoft Copilot Chat to more than 25,000 professionals, including secure web-style querying, file upload for prompt context, and agent creation, extending the same generative AI workflow beyond the original pilot.

data_flow: Employees submit prompts inside Microsoft 365 applications such as Word, Excel, and Teams. Microsoft 365 Copilot pulls context from Repsol's cloud-held company data, Internet information, and in specific workflows artifacts such as recorded meetings, supplier proposals, news, reports, and uploaded files, then returns summaries, drafts, comparisons, and conclusions directly to the user in the application they are using.
integration_points: Uploaded files used as prompt context
business_outcome: Repsol reported substantial employee productivity gains and better document output from the Copilot pilot, alongside strong user adoption and a broader company rollout of Copilot Chat.
metrics: two out of three people at Repsol would not like to go back to working without Copilot

Responses are limited to information each user is authorized to access within the organization.
The pilot tested real business situations including supplier proposal comparison and presentation preparation.
Repsol is deploying Copilot Chat to more than 25,000 professionals.
Copilot Chat is described as supporting agent creation and file upload for prompts.

"Copilot was particularly useful for three types of tasks: finding information, summarizing documents, and drawing conclusions."
"This practical research involved 600 people, who received training before beginning a four-month trial period with this assistant."

"The research also included experiments on real business situations, such as using Copilot to compare proposals from different suppliers or to prepare a presentation by compiling certain information."
"The research showed that the documents presented by people who used Copilot were 16.2% higher in quality."

"This smart assistant for the Internet 'is changing how users interact with search engines, using natural language in their queries, and obtaining more elaborate and precise answers... together with the possibility of creating agents or uploading files that can be used as a basis for prompts,' highlights Antonio Cruz."
